statements.t: Under certain clauses of our transportation services agreements with third party pipelines to transport natural gas and NGLs, if we fail to ship a minimum throughput volume, then we will pay certain deficiency payments for transportation based on the volume shortfall up to the MVC amount.

estimates.t: There have been no significant changes to our critical accounting policies and estimates from those disclosed in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025.

statements.t: “As our strategic growth projects come online and processed gas volumes continue to increase, our financial performance is increasingly driven by durable, repeatable earnings.”

Producer activity remains strong, processed gas volumes are tracking toward our approximately 2.2 Bcf/d fourth quarter 2026 target, and margins and costs continue to outperform our internal budget expectations.”
Welch added, “Our confidence in the long-term outlook for the Permian Basin has never been stronger.

At the same time, more than 13 Bcf/d of incremental takeaway capacity is expected to come online between 2028 and 2030, which we believe will unlock the next wave of producer activity, substantially improve residue gas egress, and reduce Waha price volatility.”

Kinetik now expects its 2026 Adjusted EBITDA 1 to be at the high end of its $1.04 billion to $1.1 billion guidance range, reflecting (i) gas gathering and processing fee benefiting from stronger-than-expected well results; (ii) robust operating performance that has yielded stronger-than-expected equity volumes; and (iii) commodity prices outperforming the Company’s guidance assumptions set forth in August 2026.
The capital reduction is largely driven by disciplined execution of the Company’s growth capital program and timing of project spend.
The Company advanced its portfolio of strategic growth projects, supporting increasing producer activity and long-term volume growth across its footprint.
The Company is procuring additional compression equipment to accommodate the expected producer volume growth.

With the Company’s increased volume outlook and rising CO 2 concentrations from Loving and Lea Counties, Kinetik is undertaking an expansion of its front-end amine treating capacity and overall processing capability at its Pecos Bend facility.
First, the Company committed to additional transport capacity on a new long-haul residue gas pipeline connecting the Waha Hub to the Gulf Coast, with the agreement expected to commence in 2029.
An updated investor presentation will be available under Events and Presentations in the Investors section of the Company’s website at www.ir.kinetik.com .
